name: E141
summary: E141 operated at SLAC, Menlo Park, California. This classic electron-beam-dump experiment remains a historical constraint in modern portal-model exclusion plots.
detection_principle: A high-energy electron beam strikes a high-Z target; short-lived visible decays of light weakly coupled particles are sought behind shielding. Later dark-photon interpretations require lifetime and acceptance recalculation.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered. This record includes reinterpretations of historical data in new models. A reinterpretation paper's publication year is not the apparatus operating year, and the original experiment may primarily have targeted neutrinos, axions or other light particles.

media.caption: Historical 1977 photograph of the magnetic-spectrometer system in SLAC End Station A. E141 used its 8 GeV spectrometer in 1986 to measure positrons behind the dump; this image shows the earlier facility, rather than E141 running.
